IoT (Internet of Things) in Smart Devices
Example: Your smart fridge can alert you when it detects low milk levels.
Automatic device connections for improved communication and efficiency.
Scheduling calls, setting reminders, and managing tasks.
Example: Your home automation system can automatically schedule a video call with your team at the start of each workday.

key_terms.definition: A fifth-generation wireless technology that offers significantly faster data transfer rates and lower latency compared to previous generations.
A method for making voice calls using an internet connection instead of traditional phone lines, often used in smart devices for clear and efficient communication.
A network of physical devices, vehicles, appliances, and other items embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity that enables these objects to connect and exchange data.

examples: Your smart fridge can call you when it detects low milk levels, ensuring you don't run out during the week.
A smart speaker automatically schedules a video call with your calendar app based on your upcoming appointments.
In a smart home office setup, devices like lights, thermostats, and security systems can all communicate to ensure optimal conditions for work.
connections: 5G and IoT Together: The combination of 5G and IoT enhances the capabilities of smart devices by providing faster data transfer rates and enabling more seamless device interactions.
Smart Devices and VoIP: Both technologies complement each other, improving communication quality and efficiency in various applications such as home automation and office management.
